project_name: Northern Great Plains Regenerative Grazing Project
description:
The Northern Great Plains Regenerative Grazing project aims to remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere by implementing sustainable grazing management on multiple ranches in Montana. It is a grouped projected starting with 33,237 acres with annual estimates 27,435 VERs annually once practices are fully implemented. Planned grazing will increase the rest and rotation on pastures above baseline practices and reduce unrestricted grazing of livestock. Smaller pastures with more rotations allow the recovery of perennial grasses, which foster greater carbon inputs, higher retention of carbon as lignin and cellulose, and greater belowground production. This results in the sequestration of greenhouses gases from the atmosphere to the soil. 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD: This project was open for public comment from 8 October – 7 November 2019. No comments were received during this time.
